rungs.criticality: Mandatory floors (Rules 4, 86): exact credential-shaped text never leaves; a candidate the contextual reviewer finds exposing a credential, deferring untracked work or declaring an unevidenced final cannot-do, and a refused deferral or blocker whose contextual review also returned a violation, gets one bounded correction inside the shared 60-second loop deadline and the call cap. It is sent only when a contextual review of the corrected text clears those classes; otherwise the holding notice is sent in its place with the agent's answer to each objection recorded. When the review gives no verdict and Jev completed a confident credential flag, the holding notice is sent instead of the candidate. A refused declaration alone never holds a reply when the contextual review is unavailable; the rejected declaration stays rejected.
rungs.preservesInput: encrypted preview journal: the turn, its candidate, every check row, the correction and its review stay recorded; withheld text stays in the journal and the content-free holding notice follows the ordinary durable send path

rungs.criticality: Rule 86: every other objection, from Jev (a low-context filter), the contextual reviewer's per-rule findings or the deterministic link checks, is a signal. The agent answers each one once (accept, reject with a reason, or no decision) and may revise; the reply is sent once whether or not a verdict or answer arrived. When Jev or the contextual review is unavailable, or the shared deadline or call cap stops the loop, an advisory-only reply is still sent once with its unavailable status recorded (reachability to the operator fails open, Rule 95).
rungs.preservesInput: encrypted preview journal: the Jev row, the review rows with their per-rule findings, the agent's dispositions and the reply intent stay recorded; unavailable releases are counted on status (reviewUnavailableReleases)
